title: World map / satellite-scale combat with defensible assets
summary: A literal city-scale (satellite-view-style) map that mech-level combat plays out on, with specific named assets the party has to defend, giving Claimant attacks concrete stakes. A real map asset has since been produced.
description:
Originally floated as an eventual need: a literal city-scale map mech combat plays out on, with specific, named assets the party has to defend — giving Claimant attacks concrete stakes ('defend this') rather than only abstract ones. This has since been substantially concretized by two later, more detailed ideas: civilian-protection-combat-layer (the actual combat mechanic — civilians/vehicles/infrastructure as attackable, defendable statblocked targets with an HP-based outcome report) and mech-physical-classification-and-equipment (which confirms a real world-map asset already exists: a heavily zoomed-out view of the city with a large surrounding ocean and inland mountains/plains, produced specifically for this purpose).

Kept as its own tracked idea because the 'satellite-view map as its own scene type' framing is a distinct decision from the combat-mechanics layer that runs on top of it — the map could end up used differently than the civilian-protection mechanic assumes, and vice versa.
sourceContext: User 'vibe with me' worldbuilding session — originally captured as prose in design/campaign-arc.md's 'Evolving mechanics threads' section; concretized by a later planning message; migrated here on audit.
openSubQuestions: Which specific city assets are named as defensible — not enumerated yet.
resolvedSubQuestions: How the satellite-scale map scene relates to normal battle-map scenes mechanically (zoom levels? separate scene entirely with its own grid convention?) — ANSWERED 2026-08-23 by procedural-city-map-generator: ONE vector model rendered at two scales, not two scene types. At FEET_PER_SQUARE=50 a grid square is ~15m, which is larger than a house, so individual buildings are simply not representable on the tactical grid. The city view therefore takes the BLOCK as its unit; the battle view crops a neighbourhood and takes the BUILDING as its unit. Both render from the same seeded vector scene graph, which is a further reason that map is generated as vector rather than raster.
